# AMR for R 2.0.0: reference of all functions and data sets

> This is the complete reference documentation of version 2.0.0 of the AMR package for R, released on 2023-03-12. It applies to AMR 2.0.0 only: functions, arguments, defaults, data sets and their columns can differ in other versions.

How to use this reference:

- Every function and data set has its own page, linked below. The pages are Markdown and live at `https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/<page>.md`.
- Each page contains the usage (all arguments with their defaults), the description of every argument, details, the return value and examples.
- Several related functions share one page; the list below shows which page documents which function (e.g., `mo_gramstain()` is documented on `mo_property.md`).
- A function or argument that is not in this reference does not exist in this version.
- The documentation of other versions is listed at <https://amr-for-r.org/release/llms.txt>.

## Preparing data: microorganisms

These functions are meant to get taxonomically valid properties of
microorganisms from any input, but also properties derived from
taxonomy, such as the Gram stain
([`mo_gramstain()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/mo_property.md))
, or
[`mo_is_yeast()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/mo_property.md).
Use
[`mo_source()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/mo_source.md)
to teach this package how to translate your own codes to valid
microorganisms, and use \`add_custom_microorganisms() to add your own
custom microorganisms to this package.

- [`as.mo()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  [`is.mo()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  [`mo_uncertainties()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  [`mo_renamed()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  [`mo_failures()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  [`mo_reset_session()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  [`mo_cleaning_regex()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mo.md)
  : Transform Arbitrary Input to Valid Microbial Taxonomy
- [`mo_name()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/mo_property.md)

## Preparing data: antibiotics

Use these functions to get valid properties of antibiotics from any
input or to clean your input. You can even retrieve drug names and doses
from clinical text records, using
[`ab_from_text()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_from_text.md).

- [`as.ab()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.ab.md)
  [`is.ab()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.ab.md) :
  Transform Input to an Antibiotic ID
- [`ab_name()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_cid()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_synonyms()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_tradenames()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_group()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_atc()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_atc_group1()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_atc_group2()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_loinc()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_ddd()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_ddd_units()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_info()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_url()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`ab_property()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  [`set_ab_names()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_property.md)
  : Get Properties of an Antibiotic
- [`ab_from_text()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/ab_from_text.md)
  : Retrieve Antimicrobial Drug Names and Doses from Clinical Text
- [`atc_online_property()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/atc_online.md)
  [`atc_online_groups()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/atc_online.md)
  [`atc_online_ddd()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/atc_online.md)
  [`atc_online_ddd_units()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/atc_online.md)
  : Get ATC Properties from WHOCC Website
- [`add_custom_antimicrobials()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/add_custom_antimicrobials.md)
  [`clear_custom_antimicrobials()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/add_custom_antimicrobials.md)
  : Add Custom Antimicrobials

## Preparing data: antimicrobial resistance

With
[`as.mic()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mic.md)
and
[`as.disk()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.disk.md)
you can transform your raw input to valid MIC or disk diffusion values.
Use
[`as.sir()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.sir.md)
for cleaning raw data to let it only contain “R”, “I” and “S”, or to
interpret MIC or disk diffusion values as SIR based on the lastest
EUCAST and CLSI guidelines. Afterwards, you can extend antibiotic
interpretations by applying [EUCAST
rules](https://www.eucast.org/expert_rules_and_intrinsic_resistance/)
with
[`eucast_rules()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/eucast_rules.md).

- [`as.sir()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.sir.md)
  [`NA_sir_`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.sir.md)
  [`is.sir()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.sir.md)
  [`is_sir_eligible()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.sir.md)
  [`sir_interpretation_history()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.sir.md)
  : Translate MIC and Disk Diffusion to SIR, or Clean Existing SIR Data
- [`as.mic()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mic.md)
  [`NA_mic_`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mic.md)
  [`is.mic()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mic.md)
  [`droplevels(`*`<mic>`*`)`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.mic.md)
  : Transform Input to Minimum Inhibitory Concentrations (MIC)
- [`as.disk()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.disk.md)
  [`NA_disk_`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.disk.md)
  [`is.disk()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.disk.md)
  : Transform Input to Disk Diffusion Diameters
- [`eucast_rules()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/eucast_rules.md)
  [`eucast_dosage()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/eucast_rules.md)
  : Apply EUCAST Rules
- [`custom_eucast_rules()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/custom_eucast_rules.md)
  : Define Custom EUCAST Rules

## Analysing data: antimicrobial resistance

Use these function for the analysis part. You can use
[`susceptibility()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
or
[`resistance()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
on any antibiotic column. With
[`antibiogram()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiogram.md),
you can generate a traditional, combined, syndromic, or
weighted-incidence syndromic combination antibiogram(WISCA). This
function also comes with support for R Markdown and Quarto. Be sure to
first select the isolates that are appropiate for analysis, by using
[`first_isolate()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/first_isolate.md)
or
[`is_new_episode()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/get_episode.md).
You can also filter your data on certain resistance in certain
antibiotic classes
([`carbapenems()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiotic_class_selectors.md),
[`aminoglycosides()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiotic_class_selectors.md)),
or determine multi-drug resistant microorganisms (MDRO,
[`mdro()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/mdro.md)).

- [`antibiogram()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiogram.md)
  [`plot(`*`<antibiogram>`*`)`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiogram.md)
  [`autoplot(`*`<antibiogram>`*`)`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiogram.md)
  [`knit_print(`*`<antibiogram>`*`)`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/antibiogram.md)
  : Generate Antibiogram: Traditional, Combined, Syndromic, or
  Weighted-Incidence Syndromic Combination (WISCA)

- [`resistance()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`susceptibility()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`sir_confidence_interval()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`proportion_R()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`proportion_IR()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`proportion_I()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`proportion_SI()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`proportion_S()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`proportion_df()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  [`sir_df()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/proportion.md)
  : Calculate Antimicrobial Resistance

- [`count_resistant()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_susceptible()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_R()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_IR()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_I()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_SI()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_S()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_all()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`n_sir()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  [`count_df()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/count.md)
  : Count Available Isolates

- [`get_episode()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/get_episode.md)
  [`is_new_episode()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/get_episode.md)
  : Determine Clinical or Epidemic Episodes

- [`first_isolate()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/first_isolate.md)
  [`filter_first_isolate()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/first_isolate.md)
  : Determine First Isolates

- [`key_antimicrobials()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/key_antimicrobials.md)
  [`all_antimicrobials()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/key_antimicrobials.md)

- [`mdro()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/mdro.md)

  : Determine Multidrug-Resistant Organisms (MDRO)

- [`plot(`*`<mic>`*`)`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/plot.md)

  : Antibiotic Selectors

## Other: AMR-specific options

The AMR package is customisable, by providing settings that can be set
per user or per team. For example, the default interpretation guideline
can be changed from EUCAST to CLSI, or a supported language can be set
for the whole team (system-language independent) for antibiotic names in
a foreign language.

- [`AMR-options`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/AMR-options.md)
  : Options for the AMR package

## Other: antiviral drugs

This package also provides extensive support for antiviral agents, even
though it is not the primary scope of this package. Working with data
containing information about antiviral drugs was never easier. Use these
functions to get valid properties of antiviral drugs from any input or
to clean your input. You can even retrieve drug names and doses from
clinical text records, using
[`av_from_text()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_from_text.md).

- [`as.av()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.av.md)
  [`is.av()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/as.av.md) :
  Transform Input to an Antiviral Drug ID
- [`av_name()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_cid()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_synonyms()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_tradenames()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_group()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_atc()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_loinc()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_ddd()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_ddd_units()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_info()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_url()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  [`av_property()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_property.md)
  : Get Properties of an Antiviral Drug
- [`av_from_text()`](https://amr-for-r.org/release/2.0.0/reference/av_from_text.md)
  : Retrieve Antiviral Drug Names and Doses from Clinical Text
